# Task 036 shared XML Schema dateTime Zulu conformance corpus.
#
# ONE canonical corpus drives the Rust, C++, and Ada generated validators, so
# the three backends are proven to agree rather than each passing its own
# curated subset. Rust-side tests read this file and emit the cases into the
# probe program for every language.
#
# FORMAT
#   '#' begins a comment line; blank lines are ignored.
#   VALID   <input> => <expected normalized lexical form>
#   INVALID <input>
# <input> is a C-style escaped string so whitespace cases are unambiguous;
# only \s (space), \t, \n, \r, and \\ are used.
#
# AUTHORITY
# XML Schema 1.0 Part 2 (W3C REC 28 October 2004). The pinned UCI 2.5/2.6
# schemas use no XSD 1.1-only construct (no xs:assert, xs:alternative,
# explicitTimezone, xs:openContent, xs:override, or vc:minVersion), so 1.0 is
# the applicable standard and 1.0's year rules apply -- notably that '0000' is
# NOT a valid lexical representation (section 3.2.7).
#
# Section 3.2.7.1 lexical space:
#   '-'? yyyy '-' mm '-' dd 'T' hh ':' mm ':' ss ('.' s+)? (zzzzzz)?
# Section 3.2.7.3 timezone:  (('+' | '-') hh ':' mm) | 'Z'
# Section 4.3.6 whiteSpace:  fixed 'collapse' for every atomic type but string.
#
# The UCI profile adds pattern ".+Z", which on this already-lexically-valid
# domain is exactly "the normalized form ends in literal 'Z'" -- see the proof
# in crates/codegen-core/src/temporal.rs.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- VALID -----

# Ordinary date/time with the required Zulu timezone.
VALID 2026-09-20T12:34:56Z => 2026-09-20T12:34:56Z

# Leap day in a leap year. 2024 is divisible by 4 and not by 100.
VALID 2024-02-29T00:00:00Z => 2024-02-29T00:00:00Z

# Leap day in a century leap year: 2000 is divisible by 400, so it IS a leap
# year. This is the case a naive "divisible by 4" rule gets right by accident
# and a naive "not divisible by 100" rule gets wrong.
VALID 2000-02-29T23:59:59Z => 2000-02-29T23:59:59Z

# Ordinary non-leap February date; 28 days is always valid.
VALID 2023-02-28T01:02:03Z => 2023-02-28T01:02:03Z

# Fractional seconds: a single digit.
VALID 2026-09-20T12:34:56.5Z => 2026-09-20T12:34:56.5Z

# More than one fractional digit. Section 3.2.7.1 allows '.' s+ to arbitrary
# precision, so no digit limit may be imposed.
VALID 2026-09-20T12:34:56.123456789012345678901234567890Z => 2026-09-20T12:34:56.123456789012345678901234567890Z

# Trailing fractional zeros are legal lexically; only the CANONICAL form
# forbids them (section 3.2.7.2). Task 036 stores the lexical form as given,
# so this must round-trip unchanged rather than being canonicalized.
VALID 2026-09-20T12:34:56.000Z => 2026-09-20T12:34:56.000Z

# '24:00:00' IS permitted by section 3.2.7.1 when minutes and seconds are zero;
# it denotes the first instant of the following day. It must be accepted.
VALID 2026-09-20T24:00:00Z => 2026-09-20T24:00:00Z

# 24:00:00 with fractional zeros: the seconds represented are still zero.
VALID 2026-09-20T24:00:00.0Z => 2026-09-20T24:00:00.0Z

# Extended year: more than four digits is required by section 3.2.7.1, which
# says 'four-or-more digit'. This year exceeds nothing the standard bounds, so
# it must not be rejected by a host integer limit.
VALID 20260-09-20T12:34:56Z => 20260-09-20T12:34:56Z

# A year far beyond any fixed-width machine integer. XML Schema places no
# upper bound on the digit count, so digit-level validation is mandatory.
VALID 999999999999999999999999-01-01T00:00:00Z => 999999999999999999999999-01-01T00:00:00Z

# Negative year. Section 3.2.7.1 permits a leading '-'; '-0001' is 1 BCE.
VALID -0001-01-01T00:00:00Z => -0001-01-01T00:00:00Z

# Negative extended year.
VALID -20260-12-31T23:59:59Z => -20260-12-31T23:59:59Z

# Smallest legal calendar boundaries: year 0001, month 01, day 01, midnight.
VALID 0001-01-01T00:00:00Z => 0001-01-01T00:00:00Z

# Largest ordinary boundaries: December 31, last representable second.
VALID 9999-12-31T23:59:59Z => 9999-12-31T23:59:59Z

# 30-day month at its maximum.
VALID 2026-04-30T00:00:00Z => 2026-04-30T00:00:00Z

# 31-day month at its maximum.
VALID 2026-01-31T00:00:00Z => 2026-01-31T00:00:00Z

# Second 60 is NOT admitted -- see the INVALID section. Second 59 is the max.
VALID 2026-06-15T13:00:59Z => 2026-06-15T13:00:59Z

# Leading and trailing XML whitespace must collapse away entirely (section
# 4.3.6 'collapse'), and the STORED value is the normalized form, not the
# input. dateTime's whiteSpace is fixed at collapse and cannot be overridden.
VALID \s\t2026-09-20T12:34:56Z\r\n => 2026-09-20T12:34:56Z
VALID \n\n2026-09-20T12:34:56Z => 2026-09-20T12:34:56Z
VALID 2026-09-20T12:34:56Z\t\t => 2026-09-20T12:34:56Z
VALID \s\s\s2026-09-20T12:34:56Z\s\s\s => 2026-09-20T12:34:56Z

# -------------------------------------------------------------- INVALID -----

# --- the UCI ".+Z" Zulu restriction ---

# Missing timezone entirely. Lexically valid dateTime, but not Zulu, so the
# UCI profile rejects it. This is the case that proves the pattern is applied
# and not merely assumed.
INVALID 2026-09-20T12:34:56

# Numeric timezone offsets are legal dateTime (section 3.2.7.3) but are not
# the Zulu spelling the profile requires.
INVALID 2026-09-20T12:34:56+00:00
INVALID 2026-09-20T12:34:56-00:00
INVALID 2026-09-20T12:34:56+05:00
INVALID 2026-09-20T12:34:56-13:30
INVALID 2026-09-20T12:34:56+14:00

# Lowercase 'z' is not the timezone token; XML Schema spells it 'Z'.
INVALID 2026-09-20T12:34:56z

# Trailing characters after 'Z'. Patterns are anchored, and the lexical space
# ends at the timezone, so nothing may follow.
INVALID 2026-09-20T12:34:56ZZ
INVALID 2026-09-20T12:34:56Z.
INVALID 2026-09-20T12:34:56Zx

# --- calendar validity ---

# Month 00 and month 13 are outside 01..12.
INVALID 2026-00-15T00:00:00Z
INVALID 2026-13-15T00:00:00Z

# Day zero is never valid in any month.
INVALID 2026-09-00T00:00:00Z

# Day beyond the month's maximum: September has 30 days.
INVALID 2026-09-31T00:00:00Z
# April has 30 days.
INVALID 2026-04-31T00:00:00Z
# No month has 32 days.
INVALID 2026-01-32T00:00:00Z

# February 29 in a non-leap year. 2023 is not divisible by 4.
INVALID 2023-02-29T00:00:00Z
# February 29 in a century NON-leap year: 1900 is divisible by 100 but not by
# 400, so it is not a leap year. A "divisible by 4" rule wrongly accepts this.
INVALID 1900-02-29T00:00:00Z
# February never has 30 days, leap year or not.
INVALID 2024-02-30T00:00:00Z

# --- time-of-day validity ---

# Hour 25 exceeds every legal form.
INVALID 2026-09-20T25:00:00Z
# Hour 24 is permitted ONLY with zero minutes and zero seconds (3.2.7.1).
INVALID 2026-09-20T24:00:01Z
INVALID 2026-09-20T24:01:00Z
INVALID 2026-09-20T24:30:30Z
# 24:00:00 with a NON-zero fractional part is likewise not zero seconds.
INVALID 2026-09-20T24:00:00.1Z

# Minute 60 is out of range; minutes are 00..59.
INVALID 2026-09-20T12:60:00Z

# Second 60 is out of range. XML Schema 1.0 dateTime does NOT admit a leap
# second in its lexical space; seconds are 00..59.
INVALID 2026-09-20T12:00:60Z
INVALID 2026-09-20T12:00:61Z

# --- fractional seconds ---

# A '.' must be followed by at least one digit ('.' s+, not s*).
INVALID 2026-09-20T12:34:56.Z
# Non-digit in the fractional part.
INVALID 2026-09-20T12:34:56.5aZ
# Two decimal points.
INVALID 2026-09-20T12:34:56.1.2Z
# A fractional part is only allowed on seconds, never on minutes.
INVALID 2026-09-20T12:34.5:56Z

# --- year grammar ---

# Fewer than four digits: the year is 'four-or-more' digits.
INVALID 999-09-20T12:34:56Z
INVALID 26-09-20T12:34:56Z
INVALID 1-09-20T12:34:56Z

# '0000' is explicitly prohibited by XML Schema 1.0 section 3.2.7. This is the
# rule that differs in later revisions, so the applicable version matters.
INVALID 0000-01-01T00:00:00Z
INVALID -0000-01-01T00:00:00Z

# If more than four digits, leading zeros are prohibited (3.2.7.1).
INVALID 02026-09-20T12:34:56Z
INVALID -02026-09-20T12:34:56Z

# A plus sign is explicitly not permitted on the year.
INVALID +2026-09-20T12:34:56Z

# Non-digit in the year.
INVALID 20x6-09-20T12:34:56Z

# --- field width and separators ---

# Month, day, hour, minute, and second are each exactly two digits.
INVALID 2026-9-20T12:34:56Z
INVALID 2026-09-2T12:34:56Z
INVALID 2026-09-20T2:34:56Z
INVALID 2026-09-20T12:4:56Z
INVALID 2026-09-20T12:34:6Z
INVALID 2026-009-20T12:34:56Z
INVALID 2026-09-20T123:34:56Z

# The date/time separator is an uppercase 'T'.
INVALID 2026-09-20t12:34:56Z
INVALID 2026-09-20\s12:34:56Z
INVALID 2026-09-2012:34:56Z

# Missing separators and missing components.
INVALID 2026-09-20Z
INVALID 2026-09-20T12:34Z
INVALID 2026-09-20T12Z
INVALID 20260920T123456Z
INVALID 2026/09/20T12:34:56Z

# --- whitespace ---

# Internal whitespace is NOT removed by 'collapse'; collapse only trims the
# ends and squeezes runs of spaces. An interior space leaves a literal that is
# not in the lexical space.
INVALID 2026-09-20T12:34:56\sZ
INVALID 2026-09-20\sT12:34:56Z
INVALID 2026-\s09-20T12:34:56Z
INVALID 2026-09-20T12:\s34:56Z

# --- degenerate input ---

# The empty string, and strings that are only whitespace (which collapse to
# empty). '.+Z' alone would already reject these, but the lexical validator
# must reject them first. An INVALID line with no payload is the empty string.
INVALID
INVALID \s
INVALID \s\t\r\n

# Arbitrary text ending in 'Z'. This is the case a naive ends_with('Z')
# validator wrongly accepts, and it is why the base lexical grammar must be
# checked before the Zulu profile.
INVALID garbageZ
INVALID Z
INVALID 2026-99-99T99:99:99Z
INVALID notadatetimeatallZ
INVALID ....Z
INVALID 0Z
